authors: Aboussalah, A. M.; Lee, C.-G.
title: Continuous control with Stacked Deep Dynamic Recurrent Reinforcement Learning for portfolio optimization
connection: Trades ten S&P 500 stocks with a recurrent policy on raw hourly price changes in rolling train-test windows and decides every hour, so it supports methodological comparison only.
evidence_note: Rolling 1200-hour training and 300-hour test windows (20 rounds); no schedule ablation.

authors: Adhikary, S.; Qureshi, W.; Kumar, A.; Kumari, N.
title: Event-driven Automated Equity Trading using Simple Moving Average (SMA) Crossovers Integrated in Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) Algorithm
venue: International Journal on Science and Technology
connection: Supplies moving-average crossovers as policy inputs for one equity and acts at every step: the crossover is a representation, not a trading-date schedule.
evidence_note: Crossovers are informative state inputs to the agent rather than fixed-rule trades (Section 3.2, p. 8); data are daily (p. 6); the agent monitors the state at every time step (p. 10). Baselines are a rule-based crossover strategy and buy-and-hold.

authors: Aloud, M.
title: Adaptive GP agent-based trading system under intraday seasonality model
connection: Non-RL genetic-programming agents learn trading rules from intraday seasonality patterns using six named technical indicators (moving average, trade break-out, volatility, filter, momentum, momentum moving average), a pre-RL analogue of gating trades by time structure; intraday, so methodological comparison only.
evidence_note: Does not study multi-asset portfolio selection. Corrected 2026-09-30: (1) indicator_class was coded not_established; Table 6 (PDF p.13, journal p.247) names six technical-analysis indicators used by the paper's own best-performing GP-ISM agent, not just a baseline, so it is at_least_four. (2) repeated_runs was coded not_reported; p.13 states "We execute 10 independent simulation runs for each set of an experiment," so it is at_least_five_aggregated. (3) performance_inference was coded none_identified; Section 8.4 (PDF p.14, journal p.248) conducts a paired t-test at 95% confidence on trading performance, so it is yes.

authors: Amirzadeh, R.; Thiruvady, D.; Nazari, A.; Ee, M. S.
title: A Framework for Empowering Reinforcement Learning Agents with Causal Analysis: Enhancing Automated Cryptocurrency Trading
connection: Adds Bayesian-network feature selection, drawing on named technical indicators (EMA, Bollinger Bands, MACD, RSI, SMA and others) for two of five cryptocurrencies, to RL agents trading on daily data; 'causal' refers to feature engineering, not a control condition, so it is not a date-control group.
evidence_note: arXiv version 2 (2024-08-19) read; compared with buy-and-hold and one baseline RL model. Corrected 2026-09-30: this row previously read cadence, windows, indicators and repeated runs as not established. p.15 states "We select daily data for our study" (daily_fixed); p.14 uses one 67/33 train-test split over Jan 2018-Apr 2023 (single window); p.16 runs and averages five experiments (at_least_five_aggregated); Table 1 (p.8) names technical indicators (AD, BBands, EMA, MACD, NATR, OBV, RSI, SMA, Stoch), and Table 2 (p.9) shows Binance Coin and Ripple each use OHLCV plus technical indicators (15 features), so indicator_class is at_least_four.

authors: Avramelou, L.; Nousi, P.; Passalis, N.; Tefas, A.
title: Deep reinforcement learning for financial trading using multi-modal features
connection: Compares a price-only input with price plus sentiment embeddings for a single hourly position and reports five runs as mean and standard deviation; intraday, so methodological comparison only.
evidence_note: PPO with an LSTM policy; long, short or flat position in one instrument.

authors: Benhenda, M.
title: FinRL-DeepSeek: LLM-Infused Risk-Sensitive Reinforcement Learning for Trading Agents
connection: FinRL extension with LLM-derived sentiment and a risk-sensitive reward on the daily grid; it states that RL agents are stochastic but does not average runs.
evidence_note: Short-selling posture is not stated anywhere in the paper (full-text search). Corrected 2026-09-30: the venue was labelled "ICML 2025 workshop", but neither the arXiv record (empty comment/journal-ref fields) nor the PDF's own pages state a venue, and a web search found no independent confirmation. Also corrected 2026-09-30: evaluation_windows was coded single; p.3 shows two distinct train/trade splits (2013-2018 train / 2019-2023 trade, and 2019-2022 train / 2023 trade), so it is two_or_more.

authors: Betancourt, C.; Chen, W.-H.
title: Deep reinforcement learning for portfolio management of markets with a dynamic number of assets
connection: Runs one PPO method at three holding-period granularities, two of them intraday, on a dynamic cryptocurrency universe of 3 to 85 assets; the granularities are separate setups, not a controlled ablation.
evidence_note: Corrected 2026-09-30: (1) decision_cadence was coded intraday; Table 2 (p.8) runs the same method at 30min/1day, 6h/14day, and 1day/30day holding periods, so one setup is daily and it is daily_and_intraday_compared. (2) indicator_class was coded not_established; pp.7-8 state exactly six raw price/volume features (four price, four volume, plus trade count, of which the first six are used) with no named indicators, so it is none_named.

authors: Booth, A.; Gerding, E.; McGroarty, F.
title: Automated trading with performance weighted random forests and seasonality
connection: Non-RL: a performance-weighted random-forest ensemble, fed a feature-elimination-selected panel of named technical indicators (EMA, Bollinger Bands, MACD, RSI, On-Balance Volume and others), gates trading opportunities on a fixed calendar-seasonality rule; its own Table 4 compares this seasonal cadence against trading every day for the same ensemble.
evidence_note: Performance-weighted ensemble of online-trained random forests. Corrected 2026-09-30: this row previously read the connection as having no daily comparison at all. Table 4 (p.3658) reports the RW RF ensemble's performance trading only over seasonal events versus trading every day; results in Tables 2-3 are averaged over 50 runs per model (p.3658), with asterisks denoting statistical significance at p<0.02 on trading-performance metrics against the proposed model; a backward feature-elimination procedure (Fig.2, p.3656; Table B.8) selects 23 features, including named technical indicators (p.3660), before the reported experiments.

authors: Chandra, S.; Balakrishna, G.
title: Enhancing FinRL Trading Agents with Advance LLM-Processed Financial News: An Improved Approach Using DeepSeek-V3
venue: 2025 IEEE 11th International Conference on Intelligent Data and Security (IDS)
connection: FinRL extension adding DeepSeek-V3 news sentiment to a PPO agent's state; a representation change only, with the reward and the daily schedule unchanged.

authors: Chung, J.; Kim, M.; Min, S.; Choi, H.; Park, S.; Kim, J.
title: Correlation-assisted spatio-temporal reinforcement learning for stock revenue maximization
connection: Its reward penalizes over-trading through transaction costs while the agent may still act every day: a reward design, not a cadence precedent.
evidence_note: Not evidence about trading frequency.

authors: de-la-Rica-Escudero, A.; Garrido-Merchán, E. C.; Coronado-Vaca, M.
title: Explainable post hoc portfolio management financial policy of a Deep Reinforcement Learning agent
connection: Explains a trained DRL portfolio policy post hoc with Shapley values on five US stocks with daily data; it explains portfolio choices, not decision timing.
evidence_note: Significance tests apply to explanations (50 repeated hypothesis-test runs on Shapley values), not to trading performance.

authors: Gu, F.; Jiang, Z.; García-Fernández, Á. F.; Stefanidis, A.; Su, J.; Li, H.
title: MTS: A deep reinforcement learning portfolio management framework with time-awareness and short-selling
venue: Intelligent Data Analysis: An International Journal
connection: Adds time-awareness through calendar-time features and attention, with an explicit short-selling framework, on seven indicators and five rolling annual windows; trading remains daily.
evidence_note: arXiv preprint 2503.04143 (2025); the journal version is dated 2026.

authors: Guan, M.; Liu, X.-Y.
title: Explainable Deep Reinforcement Learning for Portfolio Management: An Empirical Approach
venue: Proceedings of the Second ACM International Conference on AI in Finance
connection: Four-indicator (MACD, RSI, CCI, ADX), long-only FinRL portfolio study whose significance tests concern explanation metrics, not trading performance.
evidence_note: Significance stars attach to correlation coefficients in its explanation metric; weights are softmax-constrained (long-only).

authors: Hirchoua, B.; Ouhbi, B.; Frikh, B.
title: Deep reinforcement learning based trading agents: Risk curiosity driven learning for financial rules-based policy
connection: Trains PPO agents on raw data without handcrafted features, using self-play on bootstrapped datasets; representation-free by design, and no schedule manipulation was found.
evidence_note: Buy, sell or hold per stock; 504 bootstrapped datasets.

authors: Huang, Z.; Tanaka, F.
title: MSPM: A modularized and scalable multi-agent reinforcement learning-based system for financial portfolio management
connection: Multi-agent design with one agent per asset (EAM) feeding a single portfolio-level agent (SAM) that issues the joint reallocation action, rather than one policy consuming raw multi-asset data directly; its inputs are not established in the reviewed pages.
evidence_note: Corrected 2026-09-30: decision_cadence was coded not_established; pp.6 and 13 state decisions occur at "any given periodic (daily) time-step" and report a "periodic (daily) rate of return... at every time step," so it is daily_fixed.

authors: Huang, Y.; Yan, J.; Lu, X.; Zhao, L.
title: Explainable reinforcement learning with adaptive feature selection for stock trading
connection: Selects a compact panel of seven named technical indicators from a comprehensive candidate set before training (random-forest importance plus SHAP): a selected subset, not a graded sweep over indicator counts.
evidence_note: Selection precedes training rather than following as an ablation; whether the selected-versus-full comparison carries a significance test was not confirmed in the pages read. Corrected 2026-09-30: (1) indicator_class was coded not_established; Table 3 (p.10) states "Number of selected features, K, 7," so it is at_least_four. (2) evaluation_windows was coded not_established; Fig.3 (p.8) and p.7 show one fixed train (2012-2023) / test (2024-2025) split, so it is single.

authors: Jang, J.; Seong, N.
title: Deep reinforcement learning for stock portfolio optimization by connecting with modern portfolio theory
connection: Trades a 29-stock DJIA portfolio plus cash on three indicators with fixed ten-day rebalancing, both as design choices, and aggregates ten runs on a single evaluation window.
evidence_note: Three indicators: moving average, RSI and MACD (p. 4); rebalancing every ten days (p. 6).

authors: Jeong, D. W.; Gu, Y. H.
title: Pro Trader RL: Reinforcement learning framework for generating trading knowledge by mimicking the decision-making patterns of professional traders
connection: A Donchian-channel rule gates the entry stage only; a separately trained sell agent then decides each day for 120 days, so it is a partial timing analogue, not a portfolio-level trigger scheduler.
evidence_note: 21 technical indicators in a 69-variable state, the densest verified; evaluated over bull, bear and sideways sub-periods.

authors: Jiang, Y.; Olmo, J.; Atwi, M.
title: Deep reinforcement learning for portfolio selection
connection: Continuous-action TD3 portfolio policy with a mean-variance reward and transaction costs, compared with mean-variance benchmarks: a generic portfolio-DRL comparator, not schedule-specific.

authors: Kadia, A.; Dey, R.; Kar, A.
title: Smart Stock Trading using an Advanced Combination of Technical Indicators with Volume Confirmation Integrated in Reinforcement Learning
venue: International Journal on Science and Technology
connection: Compares six hand-picked trading-rule combinations (moving-average crossover, average traded volume and price returns; two to three indicators) with RSI and volume confirmation on ten Nifty 50 stocks at daily, hourly and 5-minute cadences: rule combinations at multiple cadences, not a graded indicator-count sweep.
evidence_note: The '10' is a stock count; an earlier note that read it as an indicator count was corrected after reading the paper. Corrected 2026-09-30: (1) decision_cadence was coded daily_fixed; the same rule strategies and the proposed model are compared at daily (Table 2, p.12, 5y), hourly (Table 3, p.13, 1y) and 5-minute (Table 4, pp.15-16, 1mo) cadences, so it is daily_and_intraday_compared and multiple_frequencies_one_method is yes. (2) indicator_class was coded not_established; p.10 states the proposed model's state space considers an SMA-crossover indicator, average traded volume and price returns (two to three named quantities), so it is one_to_three.

authors: Kim, J.; Yi, H.; Gim, M.; Choi, D.; Kang, J.
title: DeepAries: Adaptive Rebalancing Interval Selection for Enhanced Portfolio Selection
venue: Proceedings of the 34th ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management
connection: The policy chooses its rebalancing interval from 1, 5 or 20 days, so the schedule is learned where this paper's schedulers are fixed; long-only, with ten runs of which only the best-validation run is reported.
evidence_note: Portfolio weights are constrained to be non-negative and to sum to one. Also arXiv:2510.14985.

authors: Lalor, L.; Swishchuk, A.
title: Deep Reinforcement Learning in Non-Markov Market-Making
connection: RL market making with continuous quoting under a non-Markov price state built from order-book history: no trading-date scheduler and no daily-versus-restricted comparison, and intraday.
evidence_note: Actor-critic (SAC-style) agent with a reparameterized Gaussian policy, tested on simulator price paths. Authors confirmed through Crossref.

authors: Lei, K.; Zhang, B.; Li, Y.; Yang, M.; Shen, Y.
title: Time-driven feature-aware jointly deep reinforcement learning for financial signal representation and algorithmic trading
connection: About 33 indicators reweighted by a learned per-feature gate: the representation is learned while the schedule stays daily, in contrast with fixed, non-learned representations.
evidence_note: Its own ablation: removing the gate lowers total profit from 140.81 to 122.60.

authors: Li, Y.; Ni, P.; Chang, V.
title: Application of deep reinforcement learning in stock trading strategies and stock forecasting
connection: DQN-family agents on NYSE and NASDAQ daily price and volume data with indicators including the Aroon oscillator, evaluated on train-test profit: a general DRL trading case study, not schedule-specific.

authors: Li, Z.; Liu, X.-Y.; Zheng, J.; Wang, Z.; Walid, A.; Guo, J.
title: FinRL-Podracer: High Performance and Scalable Deep Reinforcement Learning for Quantitative Finance
venue: Proceedings of the Second ACM International Conference on AI in Finance
connection: Scalable FinRL training that compares daily and minute-level data as separate setups: a data-granularity comparison, not a date-control experiment.

authors: Li, S.; Yu, M.; Dossor, F.
title: Option-Driven Sentiment in FinRL: a PPO Approach to Trading
venue: 2025 IEEE 11th International Conference on Intelligent Data and Security (IDS)
connection: FinRL Contest 2025 entry supplying MACD, Bollinger Bands, RSI, CCI, DX, SMA, VIX, Turbulence and a Put-Call Ratio to a PPO agent on NASDAQ-100: a dense representation, not a sparse one; the daily schedule is unchanged.
evidence_note: Trained 2013-2018, traded 2019-2023. Corrected 2026-09-30: indicator_class was coded one_to_three (VIX, Turbulence and the Put-Call Ratio only); p.2 explicitly lists MACD, Bollinger Bands, RSI, CCI, DX and SMA alongside those three, so the correct value is at_least_four.

authors: Liu, X.-Y.; Rui, J.; Gao, J.; Yang, L.; Yang, H.; Wang, Z.; Wang, C. D.; Guo, J.
title: FinRL-Meta: A Universe of Near-Real Market Environments for Data-Driven Deep Reinforcement Learning in Quantitative Finance
connection: Earlier FinRL-Meta version: near-real market environments with a one-minute setting, not comparable in kind to a daily design; this short workshop paper never enumerates a named indicator set.
evidence_note: The expanded NeurIPS 2022 version is listed separately. Corrected 2026-09-30: indicator_class was coded at_least_four; a full-text search of this 6-page paper found no enumerated indicator list, only the generic data-category label "Prices & Indicators" (p.2, Table 1), so the correct value is not_established.

authors: Liu, X.-Y.; Yang, H.; Gao, J.; Wang, C. D.
title: FinRL: Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework to Automate Trading in Quantitative Finance
venue: Proceedings of the Second ACM International Conference on AI in Finance
connection: The library and pipeline from which the ten-indicator daily benchmark descends; the indicator set is configurable and trading is daily.
evidence_note: Earlier workshop version: bib key finrl2020. The tutorial code lists eight technical indicators; with VIX and turbulence the benchmark has ten per-stock inputs.

authors: Liu, X.-Y.; Xia, Z.; Rui, J.; Gao, J.; Yang, H.; Zhu, M.; Wang, C. D.; Wang, Z.; Guo, J.
title: FinRL-Meta: Market Environments and Benchmarks for Data-Driven Financial Reinforcement Learning
venue: NeurIPS 2022 Datasets and Benchmarks Track (arXiv preprint version)
connection: Expanded FinRL-Meta: a four-indicator daily DJIA-30 demonstration; it names optional short-selling as a configurable setting without stating which setting the demonstration uses.
evidence_note: Four indicators: MACD, RSI, CCI, ADX.

authors: Majidi, N.; Shamsi, M.; Marvasti, F.
title: Algorithmic trading using continuous action space deep reinforcement learning
connection: Single-asset TD3 agents on a sliding window of daily close-price changes, with t-tests against discretized action variants; daily throughout, with no schedule ablation.
evidence_note: Table 4 (p. 7) reports t-tests at alpha = 0.01; pairing is not stated. 40 experiments.

authors: Orra, A.; Bhambu, A.; Choudhary, H.; Thakur, M.; Natarajan, S.
title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Investor-Specific Portfolio Optimization: A Volatility-Guided Asset Selection Approach
connection: Changes the asset-selection step ahead of the DRL policy and reports five averaged runs on a single evaluation window, without an interval or a test.
evidence_note: Short-selling posture is not stated anywhere in the paper (full-text search). Corrected 2026-09-30: venue was labelled "arXiv preprint"; p.1 carries the header "Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2025", so it is a published ICLR 2025 paper, cited here by its arXiv identifier.

authors: Orra, A.; Choudhary, H.; Sharma, A.; Thakur, M.
title: Enhancing deep reinforcement learning for stock trading: a reward shaping approach via expert feedback
connection: PPO agent whose reward is shaped by agreement with a rule-based expert trend vote (five indicator-derived buy, sell or flat votes): a reward-design change on a daily schedule, with no schedule manipulation.
evidence_note: Stocks from four indices (Dow, Sensex, TWSE, FTSE). All models, including the proposed scheme, are trained five times, with mean and standard deviation reported in Table 3 (journal p. 11088, Table 3 on p. 11086); no significance test accompanies the comparison. Corrected 2026-09-29 from an earlier not_reported coding: this PDF's extracted text layer is garbled (non-standard font encoding), so pdf_search and pdf_read_pages return scrambled glyphs; the fact was confirmed by rendering pp. 11086 and 11088 as images instead.

authors: Ospina-Holguín, J. H.; Padilla-Ospina, A. M.
title: Reinforcement learning meets technical analysis: combining moving average rules for optimal alpha
connection: Non-RL econometric test of whether moving-average crossover rules earn significant alpha; the same crossover family as this paper's SMA-30/SMA-60 schedule, tested as a rule rather than as a schedule.
evidence_note: Newey-West HAC-consistent t-tests with out-of-sample validation and business-cycle heterogeneity.

authors: Pendharkar, P. C.; Cusatis, P.
title: Trading financial indices with reinforcement learning agents
connection: Compares annual, semiannual and quarterly rebalancing of a two-asset tabular RL portfolio; cited only as a fixed non-daily cadence example, because the scenarios also differ in datasets and parameter selection.
evidence_note: Quarterly, semi-annual and annual trading periods (p. 2); annual rebalancing outperformed the higher frequencies, with one point estimate per frequency and no paired seeds or multiple-comparison correction.

authors: Shavandi, A.; Khedmati, M.
title: A multi-agent deep reinforcement learning framework for algorithmic trading in financial markets
connection: Three DQN agents at 1-hour, 15-minute and 5-minute timeframes on one forex pair, each holding its position for a fixed window after acting; intraday, so methodological comparison only.
evidence_note: The holding window is a hyperparameter, not a tested ablation; 20 runs aggregated.

authors: Sood, S.; Papasotiriou, K.; Vaiciulis, M.; Balch, T.
title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Optimal Portfolio Allocation: A Comparative Study with Mean-Variance Optimization
connection: Benchmarks DRL against mean-variance optimization with five seeds in each of ten rolling windows and reports averages without intervals or tests; long-only, with no named technical indicators.
evidence_note: Five agents, each trained on a different seed, averaged per year and then across backtest periods (p. 6); ten backtest experiments over different periods (p. 8).

authors: Taghian, M.; Asadi, A.; Safabakhsh, R.
title: Learning financial asset-specific trading rules via deep reinforcement learning
connection: Learns asset-specific trading rules from raw OHLC series and candlestick-pattern encodings: a representation family with no overlap with this paper's indicators, with daily decisions.

authors: Tan, Z.; Quek, C.; Cheng, P. Y. K.
title: Stock trading with cycles: A financial application of ANFIS and reinforcement learning
connection: Pre-deep-RL neuro-fuzzy (ANFIS) trader adapting to price cycles across five US stocks; historical context only.
evidence_note: Corrected 2026-09-30: connection previously said "a single asset"; the abstract (p.1) states the trading system is tested on five US stocks over 13 years.

authors: Théate, T.; Ernst, D.
title: An application of deep reinforcement learning to algorithmic trading
connection: A deliberately reduced observation space of raw daily OHLCV, with a separately trained agent for each of 30 stocks (illustrated with Apple and Tesla), and a binary long-or-short action: a minimal-input precedent trading daily.
evidence_note: Reduced observation space of the previous daily open-high-low-close prices and daily traded volume (p. 5). Corrected 2026-09-30: connection previously said "for one asset"; p.10 states the paper proposes a testbench of 30 stocks, training a separate agent per stock, with Apple and Tesla used as illustrative case studies (Sections 6.1-6.2) before the 30-stock results (Section 6.3).

authors: Wei, Z.; Chen, D.; Zhang, Y.; Wen, D.; Nie, X.; Xie, L.
title: Deep reinforcement learning portfolio model based on mixture of experts
connection: Replaces named indicators with a spatio-temporal embedding feeding a mixture-of-experts router on SSE50 and CSI300; long-only and daily.
evidence_note: Train 2013-2020, validation 2021-2022, test 2022-2023. Corrected 2026-09-30: repeated_runs was coded not_reported; this PDF's extracted text is garbled (non-standard font encoding), and rendering p.8 as an image shows "All RL-based methods are averaged over 5 runs with randomly initialized seeds," so it is at_least_five_aggregated.

authors: Yu, J.; Chang, K.-C.
title: Smart Tangency Portfolio: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Dynamic Rebalancing and Risk–Return Trade-Off
connection: The agent's action jointly selects a risk-aversion level and a holding-period length for the next rebalance, chosen by the policy: a learned interval, the same pattern as DeepAries (S21). It also reports confidence intervals on alpha and Sharpe-ratio differences against benchmarks, though that inference covers one realized return series per universe, not training-seed variation.
evidence_note: Corrected 2026-09-30: decision_cadence was coded not_established; p.14 defines the action as a_t = (lambda_t, h_t), where h_t is the holding-period length chosen by the policy for the next rebalance, so trading occurs at a learned/endogenous interval.

authors: Zhang, J.; Maringer, D.
title: Indicator selection for daily equity trading with recurrent reinforcement learning
venue: Proceedings of the 15th annual conference companion on Genetic and evolutionary computation
connection: A genetic algorithm pre-selects a combination of eight named technical indicators for a recurrent-RL trader across 238 S&P 500 stocks: a selected subset versus the full panel, in a two-page companion paper, not a sweep over indicator counts.
evidence_note: The selected combination (eight GA-chosen indicators: IPVI, IBBI, IPSI, IRSI, DPE, IOBV, CVOL, IVOL; Table 1, journal p.1758) beats no indicators, random trading and buy-and-hold on out-of-sample Sharpe ratio. Corrected 2026-09-30: indicator_class was coded not_established on the assumption the selected subset's size was unstated; Table 1 names the eight selected indicators directly, so it is at_least_four.

authors: Zhou, C.; Huang, Y.; Kong, Y.; Lu, X.
title: Enhancing trading strategies by combining incremental reinforcement learning and self-supervised prediction
connection: Augments the daily state with a self-supervised next-period forecast refined by incremental learning: input design changes while the schedule stays daily.
evidence_note: Double DQN over six single-index instruments (CAC40, KOSPI, N225, HSI, SP500, DJI).

authors: Zou, J.; Lou, J.; Wang, B.; Liu, S.
title: A novel Deep Reinforcement Learning based automated stock trading system using cascaded LSTM networks
connection: Varies a cascaded-LSTM feature extractor within the FinRL environment (four indicators, 181 dimensions) while trading daily: an architecture comparison, not a schedule comparison.
evidence_note: State formula 1+N(2+M) with M=4, giving 181 dimensions (p. 7); backtesting uses daily data and PPO only (p. 7).
